Off Leash update 19 November 2026
items.body:
Off Leash update 19 November 2026

CHINA
•Xi Jinping opened the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen with a nuance-laden speech celebrating the “rules-based multilateral trading system” and advocating for “free and open trade” – meaning, essentially, that China should be allowed to dump its cheap goods freely into global markets.
•Russia’s Pres. Putin also spoke at the opening of the APEC summit, but his was a grumpier speech than Xi’s. He denounced Western countries as “former hegemons” and mocked Europe for being in “humiliating decline.”
•Pres. Trump arrived in Shenzhen later, and Xi gave him an unusually warm welcome and a big hug at the airport. Afterwards, Trump, Xi, and Putin sat down together for a discussion that Xi said was of “groundbreaking significance.” Trump also met with Xi and Putin separately and called Putin his friend.

VENEZUELA
•U.S. Secretary of War Hegseth paid a surprise visit to Venezuela yesterday, and met with acting president Delcy Rodriguez, who the U.S. installed after ousting her predecessor in January.
•Hegseth announced that the U.S. and Venezuela will re-establish military ties and plan to share intelligence and conduct joint trainings.

UKRAINE
•Ukraine launched another attack on the Kerch Bridge linking Russia with occupied Crimea, this time targeting the rail side of the bridge. Rail traffic was suspended, but it’s not yet clear how significant the damage was.
•A Dutch firm, Destinus, confirmed that its Ruta cruise missiles were used in the attack, prompting the Kremlin to lash out at The Netherlands: “The confession has been well noted. Is The Hague openly joining the conflict?”
•Moscow won’t like to hear that the UK is poised to announce that it, too, will send Ukraine missiles. Prime Minister Burnham is expected to announce a plan to send Ukraine 1,000 long-range strike drones later today.

MYANMAR
•The International Court of Justice (ICJ) will rule today on whether junta-run Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims.
•If the ICJ finds Myanmar guilty, it would be the first time a state – instead of a person – has been convicted under the 1948 Genocide Convention.
•It may not be the last time: a guilty ruling is likely to energize South Africa to pursue its ICJ genocide case against Israel’s actions in Gaza.

GAZA
•Israeli tanks crossed the “Yellow Line” drawn in Gaza under last year’s ceasefire for the first time since that truce was signed.
•The military described its actions as “a precise operation to remove a terror threat,” and said it was only responding to Hamas ceasefire violations. Both sides blame the other for escalating, raising worries that the fragile ceasefire could collapse.

HAITI
•El Salvador’s President Bukele confirmed that his troops in Haiti bombed and destroyed the home of Jeff Larose, a major gang leader. Bukele called the strike his “gift to the Haitian people on the anniversary of the Battle of Vertières,” referring to the 1803 battle that won Haiti its independence from France.
